title: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
name: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
metaTitle: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing in Phoenix, AZ
metaDescription: We source medical office replacement properties near Phoenix hospital campuses for 1031 investors working inside the 45-day identification window.

sections.html: Medical office is a narrow lane in Phoenix. Good buildings sit close to the hospitals, and there aren't that many of them. We walk investors through what's actually on the market before the 45-day clock starts, not after.

sections.heading: Where the Building Stock Actually Sits
sections.html:
The heaviest concentration is around the Mayo Clinic campus off Shea and 56th Street, and along the 7th Street corridor near Banner - University Medical Center. The East Valley cluster runs through Chandler and Gilbert, feeding the hospital campuses out there. Everything else is scattered single suites attached to strip retail, which we treat differently because the tenant mix and parking ratio don't match a real medical building.

Phoenix keeps adding rooftops in the suburbs faster than it adds hospital-adjacent land, so inventory close to a campus turns over slowly. We track listings directly with brokers who work that footprint instead of waiting for something to hit the open market.

sections.heading: Tenant Credit Before You Fall in Love With the Building
sections.html:
A single-tenant building leased to a large group like a hospital-affiliated clinic reads very differently than a condo suite leased to a two-doctor practice. We pull the tenant's other locations, how long they've operated in Phoenix, and whether the lease is triple net or modified gross before we send you anything to look at.

Imaging centers and surgery centers carry heavier buildout and equipment loads, which changes what happens if that tenant ever leaves. We flag that early rather than after you're under contract.

sections.heading: How We Narrow a Long List Fast
sections.html:
On a typical Phoenix medical office search we're screening ten to fifteen buildings down to the three or four worth your time. The screen runs the same way every time:

  • Pull rent comps for the immediate submarket, not the metro average
  • Verify remaining lease term against your hold period
  • Check the parking ratio, since medical needs more stalls per square foot than office
  • Confirm zoning allows the current medical use outright
  • Walk the mechanical systems given how hard Phoenix summers run the HVAC
  • Cross-check tenant credit against public licensing records

That list gets you to a defensible short list before you're burning identification days.

sections.heading: What's Actually Driving Demand
sections.html:
Phoenix keeps adding residents faster than most metros, and a share of that in-migration skews older, which pushes demand for outpatient care closer to where people actually live rather than downtown. That's part of why Chandler and Gilbert have kept adding clinic space tied to their hospital campuses, and why satellite imaging and urgent care buildings keep showing up along the growth corridors instead of clustering only near the original hospital footprint.

Banner Health, HonorHealth, and Dignity-affiliated systems have all expanded their outpatient footprint around Phoenix in recent years, and that expansion is part of what keeps tenant demand for well-located medical suites ahead of new supply. We track which systems are actively leasing in a given submarket before we recommend a building tied to one of their affiliated tenants.

sections.heading: Working Inside the 45-Day Window
sections.html:
Once your relinquished sale closes, the clock is running and your qualified intermediary needs a written identification, not a phone call. We build the candidate list before closing so you're choosing among vetted buildings on day one instead of scrambling on day forty.

We are not your tax advisor and we don't calculate boot for you. If a medical office candidate is priced below what you sold, tell your CPA and your qualified intermediary before you sign anything, since that gap can create taxable boot.

sections.heading: What Goes Wrong on This Asset Class
sections.html:
The most common miss is buying a building sized for one tenant's equipment and then losing that tenant. The second most common miss is skipping a permitting check on tenant improvements, since Phoenix and the surrounding cities each run their own review timelines. We check both before you identify the property, not after you own it.

A third miss shows up on older buildings converted to medical use after starting life as standard office space: retrofitted plumbing and electrical for exam rooms sometimes doesn't meet current code, and that surfaces during a tenant improvement permit, not during your inspection. We ask for the building's use history before we call it a clean medical asset.

faqs.q: What makes a Phoenix medical office building qualify as like-kind for a 1031 exchange?
faqs.a: Any real property held for investment or business use generally qualifies as like-kind against other real property under current federal rules, medical office included. Confirm your specific facts with your qualified intermediary and tax advisor before you identify a replacement.

faqs.q: How many medical office buildings can I identify in the 45-day window?
faqs.a: That depends on which identification rule you and your qualified intermediary use for the exchange. We hand you a vetted short list early so you're not making that call under time pressure.

faqs.q: Do I need to check the physician group's lease before I make an offer?
faqs.a: Yes. We pull tenant history and lease structure before we send you a building, because a single departing tenant can leave a medical suite dark longer than a standard office suite.

faqs.q: What happens if the medical office I want costs less than the property I sold?
faqs.a: A lower purchase price or lower debt load can create taxable boot. We are not tax advisors, so loop in your CPA and qualified intermediary before you commit to a price.

faqs.q: Should I hire someone to review tenant credit on a single-tenant medical building?
faqs.a: We do that review as part of sourcing, pulling licensing records and lease terms, but the final credit call and any tax consequence should still run through your own advisors.
